The test image shows a corn stalk cross-section with: tan/brown interior, dark black discoloration at node, and numerous small black dots (pycnidia) scattered on the stalk surface. This points to a stalk rot disease.

Top candidates: **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (black pycnidia on stalk nodes) or **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** (shiny black lesions on rind).

The reference for Diplodia_stalk_rot shows tan/straw-colored stalks with brown discoloration at nodes — matching the test image well. The key distinguishing feature in the test image is the **numerous small black dots (pycnidia)** scattered across the tan stalk surface with dark black discoloration at the node, which is classic Diplodia stalk rot caused by *Stenocarpella maydis*.
